clue.text: Eventual defeat at cards brings connection with London banks

parts.note: Waterloo was Napoleon's final defeat, and 'meet one's Waterloo' means a final undoing
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A gambler finally loses at the card table, and the loss somehow ties up with the London banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London banks' looks like the City's financial houses; it means the two banks of the Thames, which this crossing joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The structure is a road crossing over the Thames, linking its north and south riverbanks in central London.

clue.text: Optimistic movie in network: "Dream Come True"

parts.note: wishful thinking is hopeful, optimistic thinking
a movie is a film
a net is a network of meshes

explanation.surface: An upbeat film appears on a TV network under the title Dream Come True.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: WISHFUL and FILM are plain, but the network's NET has to be read as ENT, and the clue gives no signal for that shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wish fulfilment is a hoped-for outcome actually happening, or imagined happening, which is what a dream coming true amounts to.

clue.text: Absentees get less than genuine workers

indicators.note: less than the whole word means it falls a little short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: genuine means true
worker ants: crossword shorthand for workers

explanation.surface: Staff who skip work end up with less than honest colleagues earn.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker ants are a crossword favourite, so 'workers' very often means ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Truants are pupils or people who stay away from school or duty without leave, so they are absent ones.

clue.text: Stopped man with whistle whetted?

parts.note: a referee blows a whistle; REF is the short form
whetted is said just like wetted, and rain is what wetted everything

explanation.surface: Someone halted the man with the whistle once he had sharpened it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark owns up to the pun: 'whetted' means sharpened, but heard aloud it is wetted, which is what rain did.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, so having refrained is having stopped yourself.

clue.text: First hole?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a gap or aperture

explanation.walkthrough: 'First hole' reads like the start of a golf round; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for whatever begins a series and a noun for a gap through which something passes.

clue.text: Two pieces, not of a star

parts.note: the first piece: a bit is a piece
the second piece: a part is a piece too

explanation.surface: Two fragments that have nothing to do with any star in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks celestial; it is a leading actor, and the definition describes a role no leading actor plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a tiny acting role with few lines, given to minor players rather than the headline performers.

clue.text: Last stage of setter's past?

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I'm, short for I am
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: The crossword setter wonders about the final phase of his own history.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is I or ME, so 'setter's' gives I'M; together they read 'I'm ago', the setter being past.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, adult phase of an insect after metamorphosis, such as the winged butterfly.

clue.text: "A present help in time of trouble"

definitions.text: A present help in time of trouble

parts.note: a present is a gift
help is aid

explanation.surface: A line from Psalm 46: God is a very present help in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Gift Aid is a UK scheme letting charities reclaim the tax on donations, so a gift is boosted for those it helps.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheme tops up charitable donations with reclaimed tax, a gift that brings extra support to good causes in need.

clue.text: Very happy to be playing chess quietly with Paul and Edna

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around freely, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
taken as written; Paul is a fellow Guardian setter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to be quietly playing chess with two friends called Paul and Edna.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares joy to Mr Punch of the puppet shows, who is forever gleeful, so it means extremely delighted.

clue.text: Minor disturbance caused by blow during a bit of sleep

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside the other
only a bit of the word is wanted, so its tail is cut away and the start kept

parts.note: taken as written
a cuff is a light blow with the hand

explanation.surface: A small brawl erupts when someone is hit while having a short nap.
explanation.walkthrough: The bit of sleep is its first three letters, SLE, which split around CUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle is a short, confused struggle or tussle, the kind of small fracas the definition describes.

clue.text: Arfur (Daley) nearly kept by his minder seems unhappy

indicators.note: something kept by a guardian is held inside his custody, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Tel, Terry McCann, was Arthur Daley's bodyguard in the TV series Minder

indicators.note: nearly the whole name means one letter short of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Arthur Daley's name as he says it in cockney

explanation.surface: Arthur Daley, nearly cornered and looked after by his bodyguard, looks miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Minder was a British TV comedy-drama: wheeler-dealer Arthur Daley and his minder, or bodyguard, Terry, whom he called Tel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearful is close to crying, which is a sign of being sad or upset.

clue.text: Henry and Jane sound absent-hearted

indicators.note: sound here means sounds like, so the word is chosen for its pronunciation, not its spelling

parts.note: absence makes the heart grow fonder, so an absent heart is a fonder one

explanation.surface: Two famous actors of one family are said to seem distracted and heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'absence makes the heart grow fonder' supplies the sound; in a non-rhotic accent FONDER and the surname sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fonda and his daughter Jane Fonda were both Hollywood stars, so the family surname covers the pair.

clue.text: Loved one in the morning or at first

parts.note: taken as written
a.m. marks the morning hours
taken as written
taken as written
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is seen in the early hours, or maybe at the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart or lover, from the Italian for one enamoured of.

clue.text: See 25
Beg that initiator of debt be put in prison

indicators.note: being put in a place means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a cage is a prison

indicators.note: the initiator of a word is whatever starts it, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of debt

explanation.surface: A plea that whoever started the debt should be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The D goes inside CAGE, between its A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to scrounge or ask for something free, so it is a casual way to beg.

clue.text: It's all about trouble after cinema opens at movie

indicators.note: coming after means following, so the shuffled piece is written behind the opening letter
the letter that opens a word is its first one, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of cinema

indicators.note: trouble here means disturb or stir up, so the words in front are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the two words supply eight letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: A film review: the story is all about trouble once the cinema opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like an anagram signal itself; here it is fodder, and 'trouble' is the verb doing the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat Ballou is a 1965 comic Western film starring Jane Fonda and Lee Marvin, so it is a movie.

clue.text: Most newspapers mostly back a poem

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read from right to left
mostly means most but not all of it, so the end of the word is trimmed

parts.note: most papers come out every day, so they are dailies

explanation.surface: Nearly every paper is, for the most part, supporting some poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like support; it reverses. Mostly cuts ES from DAILIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic about the Trojan War, one of the oldest and most famous poems in Western literature.

clue.text: Communicating off the field

definitions.meaning: first meaning: keeping in contact with someone
second meaning: in rugby and football, a ball over the side line is out of play in this way

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the touchlines run along the sides, and a ball beyond them is no longer on the field of play.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means staying in contact with people, and in rugby or football it describes a ball that has crossed the sideline.

clue.text: Operatic realm to disallow acknowledgment in song

parts.note: to bar is to forbid or disallow

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the short word sits within the musical piece

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
ta is British slang for thanks, an acknowledgment

explanation.surface: An opera's kingdom forbids any thanks given in song.
explanation.walkthrough: Barataria is the island kingdom of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers; 'ta' is everyday British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Barataria is the imaginary kingdom jointly ruled by two gondoliers in a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.

clue.text: Chick gets back part of the regalia I left the Queen

indicators.note: going back means the letters run the other way, from right to left

parts.note: the orb is one of the crown jewels
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A young bird receives a returned piece of the crown jewels, abandoned by Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chick' could suggest a young woman; it is a young chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A broiler is a young chicken reared for roasting or grilling, so it is a chick in the poultry sense.

clue.text: Fireweed for windows

parts.note: a rose window is a round church window
a bay window projects out from a wall

explanation.walkthrough: One clue word does double work: both halves are kinds of window, rose and bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay willowherb is the common British name for the pink-flowered weed known in North America as fireweed.

clue.text: Composer is at sea in one

parts.note: the Ross Sea is an inlet of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer is all at sea, confused, within a single piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like the idiom for bewildered; it is the Ross Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was an Italian composer of operas, including The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Turn to comedian in battle scene to make changes

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the joined pieces sit within the battle name

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a famous First World War battle
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn
Jacques Tati, the French comic actor and director

explanation.surface: Swapping in a comedian at a battle scene to alter things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn to comedian' reads like an instruction to switch to comedy; it is a letter and a name strung together, and the battle is the 1914 one in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutations are alterations, especially in genetic material, so the plural noun means changes.

clue.text: Disconcerting way to produce pottery?

definitions.note: a participle; the answer is the verb, to disconcert
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to confuse or unsettle someone
second meaning: shaping clay on a potter's wheel

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a potter's verb doubles as the everyday word for rattling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to unsettle or confuse them, and potters shape pots on a spinning wheel by this action.

clue.text: Sit back after opening of "Absolutely Fabulous" man

indicators.note: after means following, so the turned piece comes behind the single letter
the opening of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Absolutely

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A star of the TV sitcom Absolutely Fabulous leans back in her seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks bind 'Absolutely Fabulous', a British TV sitcom, but they split: only its opening is wordplay, and 'Fabulous man' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller of fables, so he is a man who wrote fables, a fabulist.

clue.text: Nervy model going in without partisanship

indicators.note: going in means entering, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: nervy taken as of the nerves, neural
the Model T Ford, so T stands for model

explanation.surface: An anxious fashion model enters, taking no sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervy' looks like anxious; here it is read literally as relating to nerves. T goes after NEU.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral party takes no side in a dispute, showing no bias or allegiance to either faction.

clue.text: Heavy metal shows signs to be telescoped

indicators.note: a telescope's sections slide into each other, so where the two words meet they overlap and one shared letter is lost

parts.note: the Bull, Taurus, is a sign of the zodiac
the Lion, Leo, is another zodiac sign

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band shows signs of being squashed together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests rock music; it is gold or silver in bars. The two signs share their L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is gold or silver in bulk bars or ingots, valuable metal that is literally weighty.

clue.text: Question of yesterday's accompanist from snow-white youth and whiter gal

indicators.note: the answer is made from the following words, which supply every letter in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pure young man and an even paler girl, asked who had played along with them yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the old music-hall song 'Who Were You With Last Night?', a question about last night's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title asks who someone's companion was the previous evening, so it questions yesterday's partner.
